Scene 01

OLYMPIC NATIONAL FOREST · NORTHWEST WASHINGTON STATE · PRESENT DAY

Dyer

Man #1: you're supposed to be in charge here, perkins.

Perkins

Man #2: I am in charge.

Dyer

Man #1: these men want answers. They want to know what your plan is. This thing could kill us all.

Perkins

Man #2: we should have left two days ago. No one would listen to me.

Dyer

Man #1: nobody knew what it was two days ago. Nobody knows now.

Perkins

Somebody has to go for help.

Dyer

What are the rest of us supposed to do?

Perkins

Wait for help? Someone has to chance it and hike out.

Dyer

That person might not make the road before nightfall. Then what? I say we run for it-- split up, take our chances.

Perkins

It's suicide, dyer.

Dyer

Fine. You stay here. Tell us how it turns out.

(panting)

(grunting)

(labored breathing)

Dyer

I think it's broken.

Perkins

You got to get up.

Dyer

I can't make it.

(groaning)

Perkins

We got to keep moving.

(grunting)

Dyer

We're not going to make it.

(distant humming)

(humming growing louder)

(dyer screaming)

Scene 02

X-FILES OFFICE · FBI HEADQUARTERS · WASHINGTON, D.C.

Fox Mulder

Take a good look, Scully.

Dana Scully

What am I looking at?

Fox Mulder

30 loggers working a clear-cutting contract in washington state-- rugged, manly men in the full bloom of their manhood.

Dana Scully

What am I looking for?

Fox Mulder

Anything strange, unexplainable, unlikely, boyfriend...

Dana Scully

I don't know. I give up, Mulder.

Fox Mulder

Funny. That's what the federal forest service has done as well.

Dana Scully

Why? What happened to them?

Fox Mulder

In a word, they vanished. Or so it would appear. This is doug spinney and steven teague. They call themselves "monkey wrenchers." they drive spikes into trees sabotage logging equipment, and make life miserable for lumberjacks and lumber mills.

Dana Scully

Ecoterrorists-- militant environmentalists.

Fox Mulder

Right. Two weeks ago the loggers radioed a message that spinney and teague had gone on a spree sabotaging equipment, causing general mischief. One week later all radio communication was cut off.

Dana Scully

Do they know why?

Fox Mulder

No. The lumber company asked the federal forest service to look into it. Two officials went in last week. No one has heard from them.

Dana Scully

It appears as if these monkey wrenchers... Are doing more than mischief making.

Fox Mulder

That's what the lumber company and forest service are accusing. They've asked the FBI to investigate. I had to pull strings to get the case.

Dana Scully

An ecoterrorism case? Do I dare ask why?

Fox Mulder

In 1934, long before anyone knew what an ecoterrorist was a w.p.a. Crew working that same area vanished without a trace. None of those men was ever found or heard from again.

Dana Scully

And you suspect what, bigfoot?

Fox Mulder

Not likely. That's a lot of flannel to be choking down even for bigfoot. Come on. It will be a nice trip to the forest.

Scene 03

RANGER STATION · OLYMPIC NATIONAL FOREST · NORTHWEST WASHINGTON STATE

Fox Mulder

Hi. Fox Mulder, Dana Scully. We're with the FBI

Moore

Larry moore, federal forest service. You can put your gear in the truck.

Dana Scully

Must be pretty rugged where we're going.

Moore

Yeah.

Fox Mulder

Is that a bullet hole in your windshield?

Moore

.22 caliber.

Fox Mulder

Somebody shot at you?

Moore

There's not much to hunt around here with that ammo except freddies.

Dana Scully

"freddies"?

Moore

Employees of the federal forest service. It's what ecoterrorists call us.

Fox Mulder

Is that who you think shot at you?

Moore

Let me get this out of the way. I have no quarrel with ecoterrorists in principle. I'm as concerned for this forest and the environment as anybody. It's their methods I can't condone.

Dana Scully

Do you think they'd kill a man?

Moore

There's 30 men up there unaccounted for each with survival experience. Something happened to them.

Humphreys

Sorry I'm late. I was down talking to bob perkins' wife. He's one of our missing loggers. Hey, larry. Steve humphreys, head of security for schiff-immergut lumber.

Fox Mulder

Mulder. Scully.

Humphreys

We've got a four-hour drive ahead of us-- plenty of time to get acquainted.

Dana Scully

Get the impression we've walked into the middle of a war that's already started? Why do these men work so far up in the wilderness?

Humphreys

That's where the trees are.

Dana Scully

You're kidding, right?

Humphreys

No. Environmentalists have made sure that all the land here is untouchable. We take our timber where we can get it. Even then, we plant saplings for every tree we take.

Fox Mulder

So why do ecoterrorists target you?

Humphreys

Tree huggers are like the boys who went up to canada during the vietnam war. They're cowardly, and so are their tactics.

Moore

Damn it. Clear through the sidewall. It's unfixable.

Fox Mulder

You got a spare?

Humphreys

Right tire's history too. Monkey wrenchers call it a caltrop. Roads back here are littered with them. Indiscriminate terrorism. Can you imagine somebody spiking the roads of washington, D.C.? How much sympathy would they get?

Dana Scully

So how are we going to get to the camp?

Moore

We're going to have to hike. Anybody here?

Fox Mulder

Someone forgot to clean their plate.

Dana Scully

Looks like they left in a hurry too. They forgot to pack.

Humphreys

Find anything?

Fox Mulder

Party favors.

Humphreys

Vehicles have all been monkey wrenched. Power generator's busted.

Dana Scully

Somebody really turned this place upside down.

Humphreys

Whoever did it didn't want the fact broadcast, either.

Moore

Radiators are all full of rice. Looks like sugar or sand in all the crankcases. They really did a number here.

Humphreys

The sun's going down in an hour and a half.

Moore

Better look around before it gets dark.

Humphreys

I'll see if I can get that generator working.

Dana Scully

You were right about one thing.

Fox Mulder

What's that?

Dana Scully

Definitely wasn't bigfoot.

Fox Mulder

Look at that.

Moore

It looks like a hive. Maybe a cocoon of some kind.

Fox Mulder

Made by what?

Moore

I don't know. I've never seen anything like it.

Dana Scully

Got it.

Moore

Can you cut it down?

Dana Scully

Yeah, I think so.

Fox Mulder

You all right, Scully?

Dana Scully

Oh, god. It feels, uh... It feels desiccated, hard and dry almost preserved.

Moore

Like it's been embalmed.

Dana Scully

No, more like the fluids have been bled from its body. Almost like it's been cured. I think... It's a male.

Fox Mulder

Barely.

Moore

I'd say it's some kind of spider's nest or insect cocoon.

Dana Scully

What kind of insect could have gotten a man all the way up into that tree?

Fox Mulder

Itsy-bitsy spider.

(creaking)

(clanking)

Humphreys

Don't move. Who are you? Doug spinney. I ought to shoot you.

Spinney

Might as well shoot yourself too.

Humphreys

You're in a spot to be testing me. What happened to my men?

Spinney

What men?

Humphreys

The men who were working this camp.

Spinney

I don't know. Probably the same thing will happen to us when the sun goes down.

Fox Mulder

What are you doing?

Humphreys

This animal's doug spinney. He's responsible for all the monkey wrenching. He's probably a murderer.

Spinney

I'm no murderer.

Humphreys

You're a liar.

Fox Mulder

Let's hear him out.

Spinney

If we stand around, there will be nothing left to say. Think about getting that generator started. Darkness is our enemy.

Humphreys

What's he talking about?

Spinney

Someone want to give me a hand?

Humphreys

Now he's giving orders? I'm the one who fixed the damn thing.

Fox Mulder

It's all right. Why did you say that darkness was our enemy?

Spinney

That's when they come.

Dana Scully

When who comes?

Spinney

I don't know what it is. They come from the sky, take a man right off his feet and devour him alive. I saw it happen.

Fox Mulder

Happen to who?

(engine sputtering)

(idling smoothly)

Spinney

I need to eat. I haven't eaten in three days.

Humphreys

What kind of b.s. Story is that, huh? You believe that?

Dana Scully

We found something in the forest.

Humphreys

What?

Moore

A man caught in some kind of insect cocoon.

Fox Mulder

What happened here?

Spinney

We camped two valleys over, four of us. Three now.

Humphreys

More rats in the woodpile.

Spinney

Our truck has a dead battery. We drew straws to see who would make the hike to steal one from the loggers.

Fox Mulder

Why not just hike out?

Spinney

It's over a day's hike. No way we wanted to be caught in the forest after dark not after what happened to teague.

Dana Scully

That's the man you said was devoured alive?

Spinney

Yeah.

Fox Mulder

Why are you out here?

Spinney

Camping.

Humphreys

The kind of camping you do is a federal offense.

Fox Mulder

Just hold off a second, okay?

Moore

No, he's right. This man is an admitted felon. He could be arrested.

Spinney

What about your offense, my friend, huh? What about your offense against nature?

Humphreys

We operate within the law. We pay for the right to take those trees.

Spinney

Well, your logging crew is taking trees that are marked and protected so don't talk to me about breaking the law... Sir.

Moore

They've taken marked trees?

Spinney

Yes, sir, marked in orange.

Moore

Old growth trees? You know anything about that, steve?

Humphreys

No. You going to take this man's word over mine?

Spinney

You don't want to go out in the night. Take my word on that. It's out there.

Humphreys

If I go out that door something's going to eat me and spin me in its web?

Spinney

Yes.

Humphreys

It's too polite to come in here and get me?

Spinney

For some reason, it's, uh, afraid of the light.

Humphreys

It's afraid of the light.

Moore

There may be something to what he's saying, steve.

Humphreys

He's a murderer, clever enough to make up a story like that even whip up that cocoon to save a few trees and I'm going to prove I'm right. This is ridiculous. Where is it, spinney? I thought it was going to come and devour me. Here I am!

(zapping)

Humphreys

Come out, come out, wherever you are. Aw, don't be shy. Come on. Huh? It's just like I told you. There's nothing out here but a bunch of trees that this man values more than human life. I'm going to see him tried on murder charges.

Dana Scully

What do you think?

Fox Mulder

I think I'm going to suggest that we sleep with the lights on.

(sighs)

(zapping)

Spinney

You see this douglas fir? It's been standing here since before time and your men cut it down.

Dana Scully

Who marks these trees?

Moore

Federal forest service. You're only supposed to cut trees with a blue "x."

Fox Mulder

It must be hundreds of years old.

Dana Scully

Must get a lot of lumber from a tree like this.

Spinney

Thousands of board feet. Hell of a lot easier than taking a lot of smaller, younger trees.

Humphreys

Monkey wrenchers like spinney here are not above marking trees with their own paint.

Moore

This tree's 500 years old if it's a day.

Fox Mulder

Look at this. What would this represent?

Moore

I don't know. I've never seen a ring like that before.

Dana Scully

Those center rings are older rings, right?

Moore

Yeah. Every ring represents a season of growth. And you see these? These are 500, 600 years old. They're a recorded history of rainfall and climate. But this one, I don't know. I should take a core sample.

Humphreys

We finished with this nature walk? What happened to those loggers?

Dana Scully

We're determining that.

Humphreys

Don't you think you should be interrogating this man?

Fox Mulder

I don't think he did it.

Humphreys

I want him arrested.

Fox Mulder

He's not leaving.

Humphreys

No, not with a gun on him. What happens if his three buddies show up and do to you what they did to those two federal forest officials?

Moore

I just want to take a core sample.

Humphreys

I got families who want some answers about loved ones answers not found in that tree.

Spinney

The only crime is the death of that tree.

Humphreys

Yeah, well, we'll see about that.

Moore

Where you going?

Humphreys

I'm hiking down to your truck and get some people up here who will take action.

Moore

Steve!

Spinney

Let him go. Let him find out for himself.

Moore

This is odd. This yellow ring's got something living in it some kind of... Tiny bug. It doesn't make sense.

Dana Scully

Why not?

Moore

Well, parasites attack a tree in a variety of ways but they always attack the living parts: the leaves, the roots, the new growth rings. Even if they're borers of some kind they wouldn't be working so deep in the tree.

Fox Mulder

Maybe the wood in this ring is different. They seem to be feeding on it.

Dana Scully

Can you identify them?

Moore

It's a wood mite of some kind.

Fox Mulder

Could they have been living in that tree for hundreds of years?

Moore

No. Inner rings are dead wood. The tree's vascular system is limited to the outer few rings. They need water to survive.

Dana Scully

They appear to be hatching out of the wood. Maybe when you drew out this core you tapped into a larger nest.

Spinney

Can they build a cocoon? Right after that tree was cut down is when teague died. It's about the same time that the loggers disappeared too.

Dana Scully

You think these mites killed the men?

Spinney

Maybe they been dormant for hundreds of years. Maybe they woke up hungry.

Humphreys

Damn it!

(sighs)

(humming)

Humphreys

All right, you monkey wrenchers come on out now. I know what you're up to!

(humming)

(horn honks)

(grunting)

(screaming)

(idling smoothly)

Moore

Humphreys should have been back by now.

Dana Scully

These bugs aren't moving anymore. They're either dead, or they're asleep.

Spinney

It's the light. They don't like the light.

Dana Scully

Usually, bugs are attracted to light.

Spinney

These obviously are not your ordinary bugs to say the least.

Fox Mulder

Do you know insects, Scully?

Dana Scully

Uh, just what I learned in my biology courses. They're the foundation of our ecosystem. There are lots of them, something like 200 million per person.

Fox Mulder

They've been around a long time?

Dana Scully

Yeah, something like 600 million years-- before the dinosaurs. Why?

Fox Mulder

This tree is what, 600, 700 years old?

Moore

Yeah.

Fox Mulder

These rings represent a history of climatic changes which means that, in this year in the life of the tree there was some strange event that produced an abnormal ring.

Dana Scully

Like what, exactly?

Fox Mulder

A volcanic eruption. This whole chain of mountains running from washington to Oregon is active. Remember mount st. Helens?

Dana Scully

Yeah. How does that explain the bugs?

Fox Mulder

After mount st. Helens erupted, there was radiation unleashed from inside the earth. Strange things started to grow. There's this lake where they discovered an amoeba... That sucks a man's brains out.

Dana Scully

Oh, a brain-sucking amoeba.

Spinney

It's true. Spirit lake. There's documented cases of infected swimmers.

Dana Scully

But an amoeba is a single-celled organism that can be mutated. An insect is a complex animal. A mutation would take years to evolve.

Fox Mulder

Maybe what we're dealing with isn't a mutation at all. What if it's some kind of extinct insect larvae in that ring-- deposited during volcanic activity brought up through the tree's root system-- ancient insect eggs thousands, maybe millions of years old lying dormant...

Spinney

Until those loggers cut down that tree. That would be rather poetic justice, don't you think unleashing the very thing that would end up killing them and your friend humphreys? And who knows? Maybe us. Sweet dreams.

Moore

Humphreys might have just hiked out of here. We don't know that he didn't. Maybe we're letting ourselves get carried away with this bug story.

Fox Mulder

Yeah, maybe.

(idling smoothly)

Fox Mulder

Going somewhere?

Spinney

No, I was...

Fox Mulder

Doing auto repair? You're planning on cutting out.

Spinney

My friends only had enough gas to keep their generator running 20 hours. They'll die if I don't get back.

Fox Mulder

Why sneak around?

Spinney

The forest service guy wouldn't go for it. He'd never trust me.

Fox Mulder

He's got no reason to. Neither do I.

Spinney

I can save us all. We've got a jeep. It's just two valleys over. It needs a battery. I can be back in the morning. We can all drive out tomorrow. You got to trust me, man.

Fox Mulder

Radio's back up.

Dana Scully

It's working?

Fox Mulder

I'm not getting any reception so the receiver could be trashed.

Dana Scully

What about transmissions? Can you send a message?

Fox Mulder

I could try. This is a call for help. Is there anyone at this frequency? This is special agent Mulder of the FBI we have an emergency and a possible quarantine. Our position is...

(generator dies)

Fox Mulder

What happened to the generator?

Moore

I turned it off.

Fox Mulder

Turn it back on. The radio's working.

Moore

Where's the gas can?

Fox Mulder

Spinney took it.

Moore

He took it? You mean he's gone?

Fox Mulder

He left earlier. He took a battery and gas. He's coming back.

Moore

He gave his personal guarantee?

Fox Mulder

He gave me his word, yeah.

Moore

The man who gave you his word has made an art out of sabotage and defying authority, and is probably the man who put that bullet through my windshield.

Fox Mulder

What would you have done? We've got one chance, which is one more than we had.

Moore

Or one less.

Dana Scully

What do you mean?

Moore

He let spinney take the last of the gas. This generator's got about a quarter tank left.

Dana Scully

What about the trucks?

Fox Mulder

The tanks have been ruptured or filled with sugar.

Moore

By the man we are trusting to come back for us.

Dana Scully

We got to get on the radio and send a mayday.

Moore

Every drop of fuel is going to keep this gennie powered tonight. I don't want to wait hoping somebody heard that transmission when this thing quits running about 2:00 in the morning. Do you?

(sighs)

(groans)

Dana Scully

Mulder...

Fox Mulder

It's done. I shouldn't have let him go. Let's just move past it, okay?

Dana Scully

Fine. What do you suggest?

Fox Mulder

I don't know. We'll think of something.

Dana Scully

I think we both have a good idea of what happened to those loggers and what happened to the group in 1934.

Fox Mulder

They only found one cocoon.

Dana Scully

It's a big forest.

Fox Mulder

What would you have done?

Dana Scully

Would I have made a decision myself that affected us all?

Fox Mulder

Cut the sanctimonious crap.

Dana Scully

What do you want me to say? We might die up here. If we're lucky, they'll find our bodies spun up in a tree or they may not find us at all!

Fox Mulder

You're right, and we're wasting time arguing about it.

Dana Scully

What are you going to do?

Fox Mulder

Button this place up. If we got to spend the night in here we got to do everything we can to make sure the bugs stay out there.

Moore

I'd be careful with that. It's the only bulb that works.

(idling roughly)

Dana Scully

I can see them. You guys, look at this. Look. They're coming through the wall down where it's dark. You see them?

(gasps softly)

Dana Scully

They're on me!

Fox Mulder

It's all right. Scully, Scully...

Dana Scully

Get them off me!

Moore

Whoa! Watch it!

Fox Mulder

Stand still!

Moore

Stop it!

Dana Scully

Can you see them?! Get them off!

Fox Mulder

They're not just on you. They're everywhere. That's what that residue is over everything.

Dana Scully

I thought we were safe in the light!

Fox Mulder

We are! I think the light keeps them from swarming. We'll be safe as long as we stay in the light.

(idling smoothly)

Fox Mulder

How you feeling?

Dana Scully

I'm okay. They're oxidizing enzymes just like fireflies. Maybe that's why they cocoon their prey-- so that they can oxidize the proteins taken from the fluids in the body. What if the generator goes? Will they swarm in here and drain the life out of us?

Fox Mulder

We got an hour and a half till sunrise.

Dana Scully

Then what? It's over a day's hike out of here. We won't make it on foot by nightfall.

Fox Mulder

Maybe somebody heard our transmission. Help could be on the way.

Dana Scully

You sent that call hours ago. I mean, help would have been here by now.

Fox Mulder

Well, I'm not going to give up on spinney. He gave me his word he'd come back to get us.

Dana Scully

And if he doesn't?

Fox Mulder

We'll think of something.

(idling roughly)

(generator sputtering)

(sputtering increases)

(generator dies)

Fox Mulder

You got a patch kit in your truck?

Moore

Yeah.

Fox Mulder

Maybe we can patch this or get it to hold air. With the truck's spare, maybe we can limp down the mountain. If not, we can get on the radio and warn them what's out here.

(thunder rumbling)

Moore

See it?

Fox Mulder

Yeah.

(low humming)

Moore

Listen. You hear that? It's a car.

Fox Mulder

No. It's a jeep.

Spinney

We got to move. Let's go! Let's go!

Moore

Wait! What about the body-- humphreys' body?

Spinney

Leave it. I've radioed for help.

Fox Mulder

Where are your friends?

Spinney

They didn't make it. We won't either unless we haul ass. Let's go. Come on. Oh! Damn it! I don't believe it.

Moore

You talk about shooting yourself in the foot.

(yelling)

Fox Mulder

Get out of there! Get in the car!

(yelling)

(groaning)

(screaming)

Man

We have an emergency evacuation situation. Requesting quarantine facility for two possibly three victims with undiagnosed infection or exposure to unknown biological vectors. Repeat, that's an emergency evacuation situation. Two, possibly three victims...

Scene 04

HIGH CONTAINMENT FACILITY · WINTHROP, WASHINGTON

Dana Scully

What is it?

Man

How are you feeling?

Fox Mulder

Better. How did the tests come back?

Man

Your respiratory charts were good. We were concerned about the damage due to inhalation. There were large concentrations of the chemical we determined was luciferin.

Fox Mulder

Which is what?

Man

The same enzyme we find in fireflies and other bioluminescent insects. Our entomologists are still trying to determine the specific epithet of the insects you encountered.

Fox Mulder

Scully? How's she doing?

Man

She's still not out of the woods, so to speak. She lost a lot of fluids. Two or three more hours of exposure... She might not have made it.

Fox Mulder

I told her it was going to be a nice trip to the forest. How you going to contain it to the forest? What if the swarm migrates?

Man

The government has initiated eradication procedures. They're quite certain that, by using a combination of controlled burns and pesticides they will be successful.

Fox Mulder

And if they're not?

Man

That is not an option, mr. Mulder.
